title: Client-side and browser trust boundaries
status: AUTHORED. The surface where the server cannot help you, because the bug is in the browser.

atom_notes.A01: the DOM is an interpreter, and the sinks are its parser entry points
atom_notes.A05: sanitiser versus renderer is a parser differential, which is the whole bypass technique
atom_notes.A15: CSP, Trusted Types and SRI are configuration, and configuration is the defence
atom_notes.A08: storage, postMessage and JSON shapes leak data across origins

required_cells.why: read the actual handlers and storage before guessing at sinks
a browser is required, curl cannot test the DOM
execution in a real origin is the exploit
execution must be proven with a control payload that must not run
the webview bridge is the same class across a trust boundary

entries.name: Security header posture across response variants
entries.role: Headers are set per response, and error pages, API routes and static assets often miss what the login page has. The test is the whole surface, not one page.
preconditions: a capture of every distinct response shape the app returns
oracle: nosniff, frame ancestors and referrer policy present on every variant including errors
at least one variant missing a header the others carry

entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
entries.name: Frame sandbox and opener matrix
entries.role: Which capabilities a frame keeps, and whether a new context can still reach its opener. allow-scripts with allow-same-origin is the combination that defeats the sandbox.
preconditions: an iframe or popup surface exists
oracle: a framed page executing script with origin access it should not have
a child context navigating its opener

entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
entries.name: Storage and worker lifecycle
entries.role: What survives logout and reload. A service worker that outlives the session can serve authenticated responses to the next person on the device.
preconditions: the app registers a service worker or stores state client side
oracle: a cached authenticated response served after logout
a worker still controlling the origin after it was supposedly removed

entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
entries.name: Post message surface and target origin
entries.role: Who can send, who validates, and whether the sender used a wildcard target that leaks to any embedder.
preconditions: the app uses postMessage or receives messages from an embedder
oracle: a message accepted from an origin the receiver should reject
a message delivered to a frame that should not receive it

entries.mirror_note: no mirror row covers this entry
entries.name: Extension privilege and injection scope
entries.role: Which pages an extension injects into, which of its files any page can load, and how wide its permissions are.
preconditions: a browser extension is in scope
oracle: a content script running on a page it did not intend, with source ownership
an extension resource fetched by a web page
a permission set covering every site when the extension needs one

entries.name: Render tree side channels
entries.role: Whether injected style or resource loading can be used as an oracle for content the script cannot read.
preconditions: attacker controlled CSS or markup reaches the page
oracle: a request triggered by a selector matching a secret value
a load event correlated with a guessed character

tree.q: Does the value reach a DOM sink?
tree.why: Client side is entirely about sinks. If nothing reaches a sink, there is no class here, no matter how many sanitizer weaknesses you find.
